subject: Living-room storage around real routines
hook: Why the best alcove units hide the bottom half
ig:
Why the best alcove units hide the bottom half.

Look at most well-planned living rooms and you will see the same split: closed cupboards or drawers low down, open shelving above.

There is a practical reason. The lower zone is where the clutter collects: toys, chargers, games, paperwork. It is also the height small children reach. Put doors on it and the room looks calm even on a messy Tuesday.

The upper shelves then hold only what you choose to show, a few books, a plant, a photo. Fewer things on open shelving also means less dusting.

A worktop-height top on the closed section gives you a useful surface for lamps, which matters once the evenings start drawing in.

What would go in your bottom cupboards? Tell us in the comments.
fb:
Small design detail, big difference in a family living room: closed storage at the bottom, open shelves at the top.

The bottom half is where real life ends up — toys, chargers, the stack of post — so we put doors and drawers there. The open shelves above are for the handful of things you actually want to look at. The result is a room that looks tidy even when the cupboards are stuffed.
